newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Rundle twins fuelled by report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Rundle twins fuelled by report.

text.p: Shares in Australia's Rundle Twins, Central Pacific Minerals NL and Southern Pacific Petroleum NL, sprinted higher on Friday, their rise fuelled by a progress report on the Stuart shale oil project in Queensland.
Southern Pacific shares climbed 22 cents to A$4.12, while Central Pacific scrip leapt 90 cents or 10 percent to A$10.00. For both stocks, these are the highest levels seen for over 10 years.

In the report, the two companies said the revised estimate for stage one of the development, a joint venture with Canada's Suncor Inc, was now A$250 million, about 15 percent above the orginal estimate.
Revised construction costs were cited for the increase in the project's cost estimates

While the cost estimate was revised upwards, brokers said traders, both local and offshore, had taken heart from the fact that some progress was finally being made on a project first mooted nearly 20 years ago.
"The update this morning showed that things are getting a bit closer to going ahead with the pilot plant," said a Brisbane-based dealer.
"They are stocks that get a bit of interest out of the US and there is obviously some good support there," he added, pointing to likely significant gains if the project proves viable.

"If it all goes according to plan and they actually end up producing oil out of the oil shale, the numbers become telephone numbers in size. A$4.00 (for Southern Pacific) will look very cheap if it all works."
Southern Pacific shares closed 20 cents higher at A$4.10 on substantial turnover of 584,376 shares while Central Pacific scrip ended 90 cents higher at A$10.00 on light turnover of 34,428 shares.
